public_rationale: The March report describes Midjourney as a profitable commercial generative-AI provider with paid subscriptions and no outside investors. That contradicts the assertion that such products universally require continuing venture-capital subsidies. This conclusion treats the listed prices as examples. It does not establish that the larger AI industry is financially sustainable.
limitations: The decisive source is reporting that summarizes an interview; accessible primary financial records were unavailable.
Midjourney's subscription prices differ from the exact examples in the claim.
The result concerns universal venture-capital dependence, not every possible indirect benefit from the wider AI ecosystem.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The only reason every app has an AI feature and every AI company can still sell $20, $100 or $200-a-month subscriptions is that venture capital has not yet walked away from an industry that relies on eternal subsidies.

statement.excerpt: The only reason that every app has an AI feature or every AI company can still sell a $20, $100, or $200-a-month subscription is because venture capital has yet to walk away from an industry that relies on eternal subsidies.

from_speaker: every app has an AI feature
every AI company can still sell
venture capital has yet to walk away
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that commercial generative-AI features and subscriptions universally require continuing venture-capital subsidies.
The listed prices illustrate consumer subscription tiers; they are not an exhaustive restriction to products charging exactly those amounts.

A provider operating a paid generative-AI business without outside investors is a counterexample to universal dependence on venture capital. Historical receipt of investment alone does not establish continuing dependence.
Use January through March 2026, the latest completed quarter before the post, to assess the ongoing commercial state.
Treat eternal subsidies as an assertion of continuing necessity, not a separately dated forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that commercial generative-AI features and subscriptions across the claimed population cannot continue without venture-capital funding, including relevant upstream subsidies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented commercial generative-AI provider sustains its paid product without venture-capital subsidies, providing a counterexample to the universal causal claim.
